standard.note: S.D. Const. / SDCL 60-11-3 annual CPI adjustment under Initiated Measure 18 (2014).

tipped.note: EXACTLY half the minimum wage, and South Dakota's own Department of Labor publishes it to a HALF CENT: '$5.925 per hour'. DOL's federal table rounds it to $5.93. This file carries the state's own $5.925 (rounding down to $5.92 would underpay; the engine computes in cents and this is the one rate in this database that is not a whole number of cents).

youthAndTraining.label: Federal youth opportunity wage
youthAndTraining.eligibility: Employees under 20, first 90 consecutive calendar days -- 29 U.S.C. 206(g). Not a state figure; carried here because it is the only sub-minimum wage available in this state.

sources.title: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation -- Minimum Wage FAQ
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. Quoted: 'The minimum wage is $11.85 per hour (effective Jan. 1, 2026)' and 'Effective Jan. 1. 2026, employers must pay tipped employees a cash wage of no less than $5.925 per hour', i.e. no less than 50% of the state minimum wage. The same page confirms South Dakota has NO separate youth minimum wage -- only the federal $4.25 opportunity wage -- contradicting several secondary aggregators that publish an $8.50 South Dakota youth rate.
